clue.text: Sauce boat not completely put back

indicators.note: putting something back sends it the other way
a word not given in full loses its last letter, so PUT stops at PU

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
PUT cut to PU, then turned round

explanation.surface: Someone half-heartedly returning the gravy boat to the table.
explanation.walkthrough: "Sauce boat" reads as one thing, the jug gravy is served in; split it, and the sauce is the definition while the boat starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the tomato condiment is one of the commonest table sauces.

clue.text: Reckless mistake, throwing away a lot in life

indicators.note: a reckless mistake is one made wildly, so its letters run out of order
the A is thrown away from MISTAKE

parts.note: the word itself is the fodder
the letter to be thrown out

explanation.surface: A careless error made by throwing away a great deal of one's life.
explanation.walkthrough: "A lot" looks like a phrase meaning much; it splits into A (the letter removed) and "lot", which belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: this Turkish-derived word means fate, the lot one is given.

clue.text: Celebrating upper speed during test

parts.note: a trial is a test
U stands for upper class
miles per hour, the unit of speed

explanation.surface: Toasting top speed recorded in a trial run.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper class comes from the 1950s split of "U" and "non-U" words, those the posh did and did not use.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for a procession or arch marking a victory, matching the participle used as an adjective.

clue.text: Doctor takes this large mammal and this small one in chaotic hybrid

parts.note: a hippopotamus is a large mammal

indicators.note: the small mammal goes in the mixed-up word
a hybrid mixes things up, here the letters of CHAOTIC

parts.note: the word itself is the fodder
a rat is a small mammal

explanation.surface: A vet overseeing a bizarre crossbreed of a hippo and a rat.
explanation.walkthrough: "Chaotic" looks like the anagram indicator but is the fodder; "hybrid" does the mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the ethical pledge named after the Greek physician is what new doctors traditionally swear.

clue.text: One way to fix a stage when cycling

indicators.note: cycling sends the letters round, so the last one comes back to the front

parts.note: the letter itself
a step is a stage in a process

explanation.surface: A method for fixing up a leg of a cycle race.
explanation.walkthrough: "Stage" and "cycling" suggest the Tour de France; the cycling is what the letters of ASTEP do, P moving from the end to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: gluing with a sticky mixture is one of several ways of fixing things.

clue.text: Prisoner starts to tunnel after getting into pipe

parts.note: a hose is a flexible pipe

indicators.note: the starts of the next three words are taken

parts.note: first letters of tunnel, after, getting

explanation.surface: An inmate starting a tunnel after crawling into a drainpipe.
explanation.walkthrough: "After getting" reads as a phrase of sequence, but both words just give their first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone held captive to force a demand is a kind of prisoner.

clue.text: Problem I can have to begin with raising delinquents

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising the letters reads them from the bottom up

parts.note: a snag is a problem
the letter itself
can is slang for toilet, as is loo

indicators.note: only the beginning of 'have' is used

parts.note: first letter of have

explanation.surface: A parent's lament: raising unruly children is a problem from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: "Can" wants to be the verb; it is the toilet, and in Britain loo is the everyday word for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: rowdy young troublemakers, with delinquents as a plural noun.

clue.text: Modest little fellow capered about wearing fleece

parts.note: to fleece or sting is to swindle
an elf is a little fellow

indicators.note: the letters of capered are knocked about

parts.note: the word itself is the fodder

explanation.surface: A shy little man dancing about in a woolly jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: "Fleece" looks like the garment and "capered" like the dance; the fleece is a con, STING, and capered is just the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: running oneself down is a way of being modest.

clue.text: Briefly irritate Labour leader somewhere in Islington

indicators.note: a brief word is cut short, so ANGER loses its R

parts.note: ANGER, to irritate, with its last letter cut
the leading letter of Labour

explanation.surface: Annoying the Labour leader for a moment in his north London heartland.
explanation.walkthrough: Islington is a London borough long linked with Labour politicians; the Angel is a district in it, named after an old coaching inn.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the district around the Tube station of that name lies in the borough of Islington.

clue.text: Jobcentre at York covers application for assistance

indicators.note: the outer words cover the answer, which lies inside them

parts.note: jobcENTRE AT York

explanation.surface: A York benefits office processing a claim for help.
explanation.walkthrough: A Jobcentre is the British state employment and benefits office, so "application for assistance" fits the surface as a benefit claim.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an earnest plea is an application for help.

clue.text: Use minimal amount of special clothing for Ms Kardashian

parts.note: sp. is a standard abbreviation for special
Kim Kardashian, the reality TV star

explanation.surface: A celebrity famed for skimpy outfits using as little fabric as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: "Special clothing" reads as a costume; "special" gives SP and "clothing for" means going around.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to be stingy and use too little of something.

clue.text: Draw attention to thin trousers pocket

parts.note: slight means thin
a pocket on a snooker table, into which you pot balls

explanation.surface: Pointing out a hole in a pair of flimsy trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: "Trousers" looks like the garment; it is the verb, meaning pockets or takes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative verb: shining a stage light on something makes everyone look at it.

clue.text: Lyceum emptied after debut of Elijah Wood

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost its middle, leaving the outer letters

parts.note: first letter of Elijah

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so the first letter

parts.note: outer letters of Lyceum

explanation.surface: A theatre left deserted after an actor's first night.
explanation.walkthrough: "Elijah Wood" is the actor from The Lord of the Rings; split him up, and Wood is the definition. The Lyceum is a London theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the tree's timber is one kind of wood.

clue.text: Spoil several balls during largely boring and empty game

indicators.note: only the larger part of DULL is kept

parts.note: in cricket an over is six balls
in means during
DULL, boring, with its last letter gone

indicators.note: an empty word keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: outer letters of game

explanation.surface: Several balls ruining a dull, lifeless match.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is the cricket unit of six balls bowled from one end; "during" here simply gives IN rather than placing anything inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: giving a child too much of what it wants ruins it.

clue.text: Cryptic Raich's postgraduate qualification in magnetism

indicators.note: a cryptic version of RAICHS is a jumbled one

parts.note: the letters of the name with its S
Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A crossword setter's master's degree in the physics of magnetism.
explanation.walkthrough: Raich is a fellow Independent setter; his name, with the possessive S, is only letters to be mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for magnetism in its figurative sense of personal attraction.

clue.text: Maize's perverse fun and games with word meanings

indicators.note: perverse means turned the wrong way, so ME'S runs backwards

parts.note: the setter Maize is ME, so Maize's is ME'S, turned round
antics are fun and games

explanation.surface: The setter owning up to twisted wordplay.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter naming themselves means ME: Maize is this puzzle's setter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the branch of linguistics concerned with what words signify.

clue.text: Turn of aviator's learner to turn 45 degrees

parts.note: an aviator is a pilot
L for learner, tilted 45 degrees into a V

explanation.surface: A trainee pilot's instruction to bank the plane 45 degrees.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is visual: the letter L rotated by 45 degrees has the shape of a V.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a rotation about a fixed point, noun for noun.

clue.text: Getafix is one trading drug for very wordy customer

indicators.note: one letter is traded for another

parts.note: Getafix, the druid in Asterix, brews the herbal magic potion
H is slang for heroin
v. is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A comic-book druid dealing drugs to a chatty customer.
explanation.walkthrough: Getafix is the druid in the Asterix comics; in the English translation his name puns on getting a fix, which makes the drug in the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone fond of words for their own sake, with customer in its sense of a person or character.

clue.text: Solicitor general appears on show promoting union with counsels

parts.note: SG is the abbreviation for Solicitor General
guests are those who appear on a show
U is the abbreviation for union

explanation.surface: A senior law officer on television arguing for a union with lawyers.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, promoting a letter moves it up the column: the U of SGGUESTS rises two places.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: putting forward advice, as a counsellor does.

clue.text: Simple bit of mathematics keeping late starter in the dark

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold on to it

parts.note: a unit, the number one, is a simple bit of maths

indicators.note: the starter of late is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of late

explanation.surface: A pupil kept in the dark by maths because they arrived late.
explanation.walkthrough: "Late starter" reads as a slow learner; it is just the first letter of late.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: with no light switched on, so dark.

clue.text: His dream broken, as was 1D by Hardy?

indicators.note: a broken dream is smashed and its letters rearranged

parts.note: the letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone's hopes shattered, like Nelson's dying words.
explanation.walkthrough: Nelson's last words at Trafalgar are recorded as "Kiss me, Hardy", which some claim was really "Kismet, Hardy" (1D); the question mark flags the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The question mark flags a cryptic definition: by one story, Nelson's KISMET was taken the wrong way by Hardy.

clue.text: My wish is fanciful?

indicators.note: a fanciful version of MY WISH is a free rearrangement of it

parts.note: the letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: Admitting a daydream is unrealistic.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: a fanciful wish of mine is a whimsy, and the wishing words rearrange into it.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight: a wish of mine that is fanciful is a whim, a playful notion.

clue.text: Elderly relative may visit Bahrain regularly, a place for winter sun

parts.note: a gran is a grandmother
may and can both express permission

indicators.note: letters taken at regular intervals, every second one

parts.note: bAhRaIn, the even letters
the letter itself

explanation.surface: Grandma choosing between the Gulf and a sunny island for her winter trips.
explanation.walkthrough: Bahrain is a decoy destination supplying letters only; the "a" after it is used in the wordplay, so the definition starts at "place".
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this Canary Island off West Africa is a favourite resort for winter sunshine.

clue.text: No time for speaker to get angry

indicators.note: having no time for something means not wanting it around

parts.note: a Tannoy is a loudspeaker system, from the brand name
T for time, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A public speaker too rushed and irritated to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tannoy is the British name for a public-address loudspeaker, from the company that made them.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with get in its sense of cause: to make someone cross.

clue.text: Diamond ring acquired by extremely rich doctor

indicators.note: the extremes of rich are its first and last letters

parts.note: outer letters of rich
O is ring-shaped
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A wealthy physician buying a diamond ring.
explanation.walkthrough: "Diamond ring" reads as one piece of jewellery; the diamond is the shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the geometric name for the diamond shape, a variant of rhombus.

clue.text: Part of forest fire remains?

definitions.meaning: a common deciduous tree, one of the parts a forest is made of
the grey powder left in the grate once a fire has burnt out

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests what is left after a forest fire; the two halves are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: a common forest tree, and the powdery residue left after burning.

clue.text: Small country's itinerant Romanians

indicators.note: itinerant means wandering, so the letters wander out of order

parts.note: the letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: A tiny state's population of travelling Romanians.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for "is", joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the tiny republic inside Italy is one of the world's smallest countries.

clue.text: Hipbone is losing its upper mobility first of all

indicators.note: the first letter of each of the words before it

parts.note: Is Losing Its Upper Mobility

explanation.surface: A hip that is stiffening, so the patient can no longer move the upper body freely.
explanation.walkthrough: "Losing its upper" looks like an instruction to drop a first letter; it is just one of the words whose initials spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the anatomical name for the broad upper bone of the pelvis.

clue.text: Cutters' chief engineer on board recruits youth leaving Oxford University

indicators.note: when someone leaves they are no longer there, so OU departs from YOUTH

parts.note: SS, steamship, the usual crossword ship
the abbreviation for chief engineer
YOUTH without OU, the Open University

explanation.surface: The head engineer of a revenue cutter taking on a young recruit who has dropped out of Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: Cutters are ships as well as blades, which is why the surface is nautical; OU here is simply the letters O and U.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: long-bladed mowing tools are cutters.

clue.text: What a Bonsai grower avoids is said to be intolerance

indicators.note: what is said is what is heard spoken

parts.note: a bonsai grower keeps trees small, so avoids a bigger tree

explanation.surface: A gardener's avoidance of large plants passed off as prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: Bonsai is the Japanese art of keeping trees miniature.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: prejudiced refusal to accept other people's views.
